where d written over τ in M signifies ἀρτιδρόποις [freshly plucked]. The scholiast explains both readings, κλαυτὸν δ᾽ ἀρτιδρόποις [lamentable for the freshly plucked]: if with τ, ἀρτιτρόποις [recently turned], those recently turned from girlhood and having reached puberty; but if with δ, ἀρτιδρόποις [freshly plucked], those just being plucked. And for those past their prime, he says, there will be weeping, or, for those changing the hateful road of captivity there will be tears.
